x: One of the great surprises of the race was the easy way in which Ring kept with the leaders. In fact, at two miles he looked capable of taking the lead, but Sid's turn was not yet, and gradually Penny, Allum and Jordan drew away from the field.
This left Allum, Shaw and Ring together. In the closing stages, last year's race was repeated, Allum again winning by a small margin from Shaw.
Rumours were flying around that a fellow named "Ring" was after somebody's blood, and then some! Within a few minutes we were lined up and off on our own individual "tear-ups."
Syd Ring and Bert Cook were on the virtual scratch mark of one minute and to Ring falls the honour of doing the fastest time, viz., 29 min. 41 sec.

Ring was laying on the shoulder of the leader, well away from the rest, and running strongly. Comig back to the starting field after a gruelling climb up the field-path, Waldock (Mitcham) was just leading Ring, wtih Constable (Croydon) third, and the ultimate winner 5th.

When the field was sighted, for the turn home, Carter was leading the pack, running comfortably, followed by Ring, Shields, Rice, and J. Flower, with our "South of the Thames" Juniors, Martin, Saunders and Chantler, close on their heels.

When the competitors did come along, Penny was nearly hundred yards ahead of Ginty and he in turn was about the same distance in front of a hot little trio consisting of Footer, Allum and Carter, followed a little later by Ring and Shields.

When seen at the end of about a mile and a half the field was led by Close (Reading) followed by a bunch including Cohen (Ashcombe) and Pell (Herne Hill). Our first man was Bill Rice 21st, then Patience 26th, followed by Walker, Duffett, Ring, Webb, F.
Carter leads Footer by a yard at the top of Copse Hill, and they stride up the steep incline like two horses, with no sign of fatigue. Then come Jack Flower, Shields, Allum, Ring D.
Comrade Ring, however, has a 4½ mile plan and is not greatly concerned with what the young pursuer is doing. As we lose sight of them they are climbing a slight hill.
We hope to fare well in the four remaining events and repeat our win of last year in the League. The men to represent us were: 3 miles, Ring (4); Carter (7); Allum (10); Ginty (11): and 440 yards, R.
Tom Scrimshaw ran brilliantly to finish second in the 880 yards race; and Syd Ring finished fifth in the 3 miles event. These two men placed us ninth of the twelve competing clubs.

Here Penny was leading Les Cohen by 39 secs., with Allum a further 20 secs. behind in third place. Williams, Taylor, Ring, Shields and Flower followed. Then came a batch of runners, led by our Captain, H.E.F.

Ring, the Ruthless, gave a great exhibition of Eastern passion in contrast to his partner, Cecil Penny, who danced with utter abandon. La Josephine, and our friend Ali, put in some fine work, although I am inclined to think the scales were faked when they weighed in!
Our Junior Champion, Ted Stimpson, was in the first 10; Alec Patience and Syd Ring were lying handy in the early twenties, with the rest of ours strung out to about the eighties.

We shall recall the Indolence that was Rollins' the Intrepidity that was Ring (he's had his teeth drawn now, though!), the Inscrutability that was Scrimshaw, the Immensity that was Ben May, and Illogicality that was Wright!
As is usual the cracks set the pace, Penny, Cohen (who is showing improved form this year) leading, Ring, Taylor, Stimpson and Parker being bunched just behind.

Penny was next, followed by Carter, Cohen, Ring, and Wood (who won the Surrey Junior Race the week after) in the first twenty places. Our hopes of repeating our win of last year were now very bright; and we next saw the field coming round Tattenham Corner led by Bert Footer, followed by Belton.
From the very start Pat Parker looked the winner and after the first mile he was leading, but followed very closely by Carter, Cohen, Stimpson and Ring, with the rest of the field in hot pursuit.

Syd Ring was the next entrusted with the baton, and at the end of his stage it was still in our possession. Owing to a misunderstanding, the change-over was made on the lower road instead of on the higher path outside "The Half Moon Hotel." Accordingly, the times issued can only be regarded as appro…
Herbert continued his good running by winning with Syd Ring and Jack Flower in the next two positions. Scoring 12 aside, the points were—Belgrave H. 151, R.N. & R.M. 274, Met.
When they reached the far corner, Smart led Cohen by a yard with Carter and Verney just behind, followed by Arthur Penny, Harry Shields, Jerman, Herbert, Ring, Taylor, Frank Webb and Lucas.
Ring travelled up from Oxford, but Len. Herbert, coming down from Staffordshire, arrived too late to start.
In the Marathon, which we had seen in the distance most of the afternoon, we had the distinction of supplying the second man home in Sydney Ring.

At about 7 miles Sid Ring had a substantial lead, but at about 15, Richards (Mitcham) with Mick Walker in attendance, were in front. Despite every effort, Mick was unable to pass Richards, but pushed him to a record for the course, Mick being a matter of a few yards behind in 2 hrs. 49 secs., a time…

Sid Ring was 5th in 2.6.15 and Fred White completed the team in 8th position in 2.7.38. Doubleday was 11th in 2.9.24 and Dick Towndrow was 15th in 2.11.26.

Actual times and positions of our men were as follows: 13, Footer, 2 hrs. 55 mins. 46 secs.; 17, Ring, 2.58.48; 22, Smith, 3.3.4; 28, Chantler, 3.5.11; 39, Pearson, 3.10.40; 40, Porter, 3.10.50; 56, Whitehead, 3.17.28; 76, Doubleday, 3.23.9; 80, McDonald, 3.25.7.

Les Stokell won the individual race with Syd Ring third and Bert Footer fourth. Bert was running for our “ B ” team, otherwise we should have scored a hollow win in the team race but even so we still came out winners and Syd Ring also took 2nd prize in the individual handicap race.
Our first man home was Dick Tobin who had been troubled by cramp in the Upminster race and then followed Bert Smith and Syd Ring who came in together.

Ring, the Ruthless, gave a great exhibition of Eastern passion in contrast to his partner, Cecil Penny, who danced with utter abandon. La Josephine, and our friend Ali, put in some fine work, although I am inclined to think the scales were faked when they weighed in!".

Penny was next, followed by Carter, Cohen, Ring, and Wood (who won the Surrey Junior Race the week after) in the first twenty places. Our hopes of repeating our win of last year were now very bright; and we next saw the field coming round Tattenham Corner led by Bert Footer.
This left Allum, Shaw and Ring together. In the closing stages, last year's race was repeated, Allum again winning by a small margin from Shaw.
The Captain that day was Bert Footer and the rest of the team were Allum, Carter, Flower, Ginty, Parker, Patience; Shaw, Ring, Rice, Shields and Taylor.
